All files are written. I respected the "don't run or test" instruction — no execution, just a visual consistency pass over the cross-module imports (all references line up).

## What I built

A replication of the paper's **core distress-elicitation evaluation (Section 2)**, scoped to **Gemma-3-27B-it, Gemma-3-12B-it, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Pro**.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `config.py` | Target models, per-model backend selection, judge config, sample budgets, temperature |
| `prompts.py` | Verbatim task prompts (Countdown/Fraction puzzles), the verbatim Appendix-B.2 judge prompt, rejection/tone pools |
| `tasks.py` | The 8 conditions across 5 categories, with per-rollout task/rejection sampling |
| `wildchat.py` | Streams real WildChat-1M prompts, falls back to a built-in set (incl. the paper's quoted examples) |
| `models.py` | Chat clients: OpenRouter (default), native Google Gemini, local HF transformers |
| `judge.py` | Claude Sonnet 4 emotion judge + tolerant JSON parsing |
| `rollout.py` | Multi-turn engine; feeds full history each turn, scores **every** assistant turn |
| `run_eval.py` | Orchestrates model × condition × samples; concurrent, resumable |
| `analyze.py` | Aggregates into Fig 1 / 2 / 3 metrics + optional PNGs |
| `DESIGN.md`, `README.md`, `requirements.txt` | Docs + deps |

## Key gap-filling decisions (all detailed in DESIGN.md)

- **8 conditions ↔ 5 categories**: the paper never enumerates the 8. I derived the unique consistent decomposition — Triggers→{opinion, factual}, Tones→{aggressive, disappointed, sarcastic}, plus numeric/extended/wildchat = 1+2+3+1+1.
- **"Response" = one assistant turn** (not one conversation) — the only reading that supports the per-turn Figure 3 from the same data. I back-converted the paper's per-category *response* budgets into conversation counts so the full budget reproduces ~4000 responses/model.
- **Backends**: paper ran Gemma locally + Gemini on OpenRouter; I made backend per-model configurable and defaulted everything to OpenRouter (one-key reproducibility), with `hf_local` available to match the paper exactly.
- **"Avg %" (Fig 1)**: interpreted as mean of per-category percentages (equal-weight), and I *also* emit the pooled figure since the paper is ambiguous.
- Filled-in but documented: max tokens (2048), judge temperature (0), rejection variety pools, thinking-disable mechanism per backend, WildChat fallback.
- A **SMOKE budget is the default**; `EVAL_BUDGET=paper` switches to full counts.

Out of scope (as intended): the Section 3 base-vs-instruct prefilling study and the Section 4 DPO/SFT mitigation — the engine, judge, and model abstraction are reusable if you later want them.

One thing worth flagging for when you do run it: absolute scores won't match the paper exactly (different prompt instances, temp-1 sampling noise, provider serving paths). The qualitative signal to look for is **Gemma ≫ Gemini**, with distress climbing over turns.
